idea.body: When a line, a transversal, crosses two parallel lines, it makes eight angles that come in matching families. Angles in the same corner at each crossing are corresponding angles, and they are always congruent. Angles between the two parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal, are alternate interior angles, also always congruent. Angles between the lines, on the same side, are consecutive interior angles, and they are always supplementary, adding to 180 degrees. A drone flying a straight path over two parallel fence lines makes exactly this pattern of angles. If just one of these pairs turns out true, the two lines themselves must be parallel.

figure.alt: Two parallel lines cut by a transversal, with all eight angles numbered 1 through 8.

workedExample.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Angle 3 measures 74 degrees. Find angle 5, which is alternate interior to it.
steps: Angle 3 and angle 5 are on opposite sides of the transversal, both between the parallel lines.
That makes them alternate interior angles.
Alternate interior angles are always congruent when the lines are parallel.
So angle 5 also measures 74 degrees.

figure.alt: Two parallel lines cut by a transversal, angle 3 marked 74 degrees and angle 5 marked as the alternate interior angle.

ways.name: Alternate interior angles
ways.when: Use this when both angles sit between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal.
steps: A drone's flight path crosses two parallel fence lines like a transversal.
Angle 3 and angle 5 sit between the two lines, on opposite sides of the transversal.
That makes them alternate interior angles.
Alternate interior angles are always congruent when the lines are parallel.
ways.example: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Angle 3 measures 68 degrees. Find angle 5, its alternate interior angle.
ways.trap: Picking the angle on the same side of the transversal instead of the opposite side.

ways.name: Corresponding angles
ways.when: Use this when the two angles sit in the same corner at each crossing, like the letter F.
steps: A drone's flight path again crosses the two parallel fence lines.
Angle 1 and angle 5 sit in the same corner position at each crossing.
That makes them corresponding angles.
Corresponding angles are always congruent when the lines are parallel.

ways.name: Consecutive interior angles
ways.when: Use this when both angles sit between the lines, on the same side of the transversal, like the letter C.
steps: A drone's flight path crosses the two parallel fence lines once more.
Angle 3 and angle 6 sit between the two lines, on the same side of the transversal.
That makes them consecutive interior angles.
Consecutive interior angles are always supplementary, adding to 180 degrees.
Subtract: 180 minus 112 is 68.

ways.name: Prove the lines are parallel
ways.when: Use this when you are given one true angle pair and must show the lines are parallel.
steps: A transversal crosses two lines, making angle 3 and angle 5 on opposite interior sides.
Angle 3 measures 55 degrees and angle 5 also measures 55 degrees.
If one pair of alternate interior angles is congruent, the lines must be parallel.
The two angles are equal, so the lines are parallel.
ways.example: A transversal crosses two lines. Angle 3 and angle 5, alternate interior angles, both measure 55 degrees. Are the lines parallel?
ways.trap: Assuming every angle pair must match before concluding the lines are parallel, when just one true pair is enough.
